newsitem.title: UK: Bildt welcomes Clinton pledge on Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Bildt welcomes Clinton pledge on Bosnia.

text.p: International mediator Carl Bildt on Friday warmly welcomed President Bill Clinton's announcement that U.S. troops would participate in a follow-up force in Bosnia next year.
"This is good news for Bosnia," Bildt said in a statement issued by an aide in London.
"It means that all efforts to realise the promise of the Peace Agreement and achieve political progress...can take place in an atmosphere of security and confidence.".

Earlier in Washington, Clinton said the United States had agreed in principle to take part in a follow-up international military force to help cement peace in Bosnia next year. He said this could amount to around 8,500 U.S. troops.

His statement follows a day after Bosnia's three co-presidents agreed with world powers meeting in Paris on a detailed plan to stabilise peace in the former Yugoslav republic over the next two years as a condition for continuing aid.
Bildt, a former Swedish prime minister, is currently in Stockholm.
